otc_advice.Fungal infection: Apply antifungal cream (Clotrimazole). Keep the area clean and dry.
otc_advice.Allergy: Take an antihistamine such as Loratadine or Cetirizine. Avoid known allergens.
otc_advice.Common Cold: Rest, drink fluids, and take Paracetamol for fever or body aches.
otc_advice.Chicken pox: Use Calamine lotion for itching. Take Paracetamol for fever. Do NOT use aspirin.
otc_advice.Acne: Wash face with a salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide cleanser twice daily.
otc_advice.Psoriasis: Moisturise regularly. Use mild hydrocortisone cream for flare-ups.
otc_advice.Impetigo: Keep sores clean. Use antiseptic cream. See a clinic if spreading.
otc_advice.Gastroenteritis: Drink oral rehydration salts (ORS) frequently. Eat bland foods like rice and toast.
otc_advice.Migraine: Rest in a dark quiet room. Take Ibuprofen or Paracetamol at onset.
otc_advice.Peptic ulcer diseae: Take antacids for short-term relief. Avoid spicy food, alcohol, and NSAIDs.
otc_advice.Drug Reaction: Stop the suspected medication immediately. Take antihistamine for mild rash.
otc_advice.Varicose veins: Elevate legs when resting. Wear compression stockings. Avoid standing for long periods.
otc_advice.Hypothyroidism: See a clinic for thyroid function tests. Avoid self-medicating.
otc_advice.Hyperthyroidism: See a clinic promptly. Avoid caffeine and stimulants.
otc_advice.Hypoglycemia: Eat or drink something sugary immediately (juice, glucose tablets, sweet tea).
otc_advice.Osteoarthristis: Take Ibuprofen or Paracetamol for pain. Apply ice or heat to the joint.
otc_advice.Arthritis: Take Ibuprofen or Paracetamol. Rest affected joints. See a clinic for ongoing care.
otc_advice.Urinary tract infection: Drink plenty of water. Take urinary alkalinisers. See a clinic for antibiotics.
otc_advice.Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Take antacids after meals. Avoid lying down after eating. Avoid spicy food.
otc_advice.Bronchial Asthma: Use your reliever inhaler if you have one. Seek medical care promptly.
otc_advice.Default: Monitor your symptoms. If they worsen or persist beyond 2 days, visit a clinic.
